sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet 8 Status
sections.summary: Devnet 8 is public, running well with minor orphan blocks; a few clients still need to move to trunk branches.
sections.body:
- Devnet 8 is performing well with only a few minor issues (orphan blocks); several builders and validators have joined including external block builders
- The network is public and teams are encouraged to join and do light chaos testing
- Most clients have moved to trunk branches, but Nimbus EL, Reth, and Grandine (CL side) still need to do so
  - This is a blocker for the upcoming non-finality test networks
- An eth/72 issue was found on devnet 8; added as a separate agenda item for the EL breakout
- No known direct block builders (e.g., relay-connected builders) are testing on devnet 8 yet; Justin Traglia to follow up

sections.heading: Devnet 9 (Non-Finality Network) Planning
sections.summary: Devnet 9 is a ~1,000-node non-finality network launching tomorrow morning European time after a smoke test.
sections.body:
- Parithosh is running a smoke test with trunk branches from every client; clients asked to confirm their branch readiness on the Steel Discord server
- Once the smoke test passes, roughly 1,000 nodes will be spun up
- Blobs will be enabled approximately 10 hours into the network
- Genesis is set to start tomorrow morning European time
- The network is not public and will only run for a few days
- Discussion on whether non-finality testing needs heavy EL state:
  - Potuz argued that meaningful ePBS/CL testing requires large EL state and heavy block execution to reproduce split-view scenarios
  - Parithosh noted that a mainnet shadow fork at 1,000-node scale is too expensive; heavy-state testing will happen on a smaller mainnet shadow fork separately
  - Agreement: non-finality network will proceed with clean/small EL state; heavy-state testing deferred to mainnet shadow fork

sections.heading: Mainnet Shadow Fork for snap/2 Testing
sections.summary: A Sepolia shadow fork will come first for snap/2 testing, with mainnet shadow fork to follow; timeline is mid-to-end September.
sections.body:
- Toni proposed a mainnet shadow fork to test snap/2 with more history, originating from discussion with Gary and Karim
- Parithosh suggested starting with a Sepolia shadow fork first (already planned), then moving to mainnet shadow fork
  - Sepolia shadow fork timing: after agreeing on testnet date, waiting for client releases, and batching with that
- Besu has a first version of snap/2 ready for testing; ethrex reported ready; Nethermind needs one more PR (merging soon)
- No clients reported being unready for snap/2 testing
- Karim asked about reorg testing for block access list healing; Parithosh confirmed reorgs can be triggered easily using a modified Nethermind fork
  - For deeper reorgs (past first pivot block), Hive is the better testing venue
- Toni and clients confirmed mid-to-end September timeline is acceptable
- Hive Glamsterdam readiness: some nits still to iron out per [hive dashboard](https://hive.ethpandaops.io/#/group/glamsterdam)

sections.heading: MAX_SIGNED_INCLUSION_LIST_SIZE Increase
sections.summary: Barnabas proposed raising the P2P message size limit from ~8 KiB to ~41 KiB; decision deferred to async PR review.
sections.body:
- The current MAX_SIGNED_INCLUSION_LIST_SIZE (8,348 bytes) was calculated assuming a single transaction in the inclusion list
- With Progressive SSZ, the actual upper bound for a list of minimum-size (1-byte) transactions is 41,112 bytes
- Toni argued 8 KiB is fine since calldata is static and blobs don't contribute to IL transaction size; also noted larger limits double worst-case propagation in equivocation scenarios (currently 256 KiB total)
- Jihoon clarified this is about the P2P object size, not the inclusion list content limit itself, which remains 8 KiB
- A related proposal adds a new gossip rule checking whether any transaction in the IL is empty
- No decision made; discussion deferred to the CL breakout and async PR review
- Inclusion list equivocation is not slashable but can be ignored with proof; full ILs are needed to verify signatures

sections.heading: EIP-8037 Self-Destruct State Gas Refill
sections.summary: Decision: no self-destruct state gas refill change for Glamsterdam; complexity and self-destruct deprecation path outweigh the benefit.
sections.body:
- Two EIP-8037 issues were raised by Pawel from a partial review; the self-destruct refill issue and a cross-frame gas laundering bug
- **Self-destruct refill issue**: Create-and-self-destruct-in-same-transaction pattern charges state gas for contract creation but does not refill it when the contract is destroyed
  - Pawel argued the pattern is compatible with state gas intent (no net state increase) and is actively used on mainnet (~1,500 accounts/day)
  - Maria countered that the refill was deliberately removed in April for simplicity and to avoid incentivizing continued self-destruct usage; a proper ephemeral state mechanism should be introduced in a future fork instead
  - Implementation is "not trivial" — requires checking original account state at end of transaction, and edge cases exist (e.g., balance sent after self-destruct scheduling)
- Client positions on the self-destruct refill:
  - Geth (Gary): prefers not to do it given approaching fork; would need more time to evaluate complexity
  - Nethermind: needs time, deferred
  - Besu: needs time to consider
  - Erigon (Milen): deferred to Pawel but noted poor deprecation process for self-destruct
  - Reth (Dragan): too late to change for Glamsterdam; re-evaluate for Hegota
  - ethrex: agrees with Reth and Geth, not worth solving now
- Consensus: no support from client teams to implement the self-destruct refill change; decision is **no-go for Glamsterdam**
- Broader discussion on self-destruct deprecation process:
  - Self-destruct removal is PFI'd for Hegota ([EIP-3298](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6049) referenced for deprecation history)
  - Multiple participants noted the deprecation was handled in reverse — alternative should have been introduced before making the feature more expensive
  - State savings from self-destruct measured as less than 200MB/year
  - Two companies identified as using the create-self-destruct pattern for user deposit sweeping

sections.heading: EIP-8037 Cross-Frame Gas Refill Bug
sections.summary: A spec bug allows gas laundering from gas-left to reservoir across frames; decision deferred to async discussion and ACDC Thursday.
sections.body:
- Pawel identified that the state gas refill mechanism works correctly within a single frame but not across frames, allowing regular gas to be "laundered" into state gas (reservoir) at frame boundaries
  - The EIP's stated invariant — that regular gas cannot be transmuted into state gas — is not fully enforced
  - This was partially fixed in earlier spec revisions but only locally, not transaction-wide
- The proposed fix ([EIP PR #12265](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12265)) would adjust post-frame gas accounting to refill to the correct counter (gas-left vs reservoir)
- Maria clarified this is a consensus-breaking change: different execution outcomes are possible, meaning blocks could produce different state roots
  - Parithosh noted this could break sync for nodes applying the change against historical blocks
- Implementation impact described as small by Pawel but clients were not confident without deeper review
- Client positions:
  - Geth (Gary): semantically correct but needs to evaluate complexity and edge cases; prefers deferral to ACDC
  - Nethermind (Łukasz): needs to consult with Ben, their EIP-8037 champion
  - Besu (Luis): interested in security impact analysis; raised question about whether child frame should be beneficiary of refilled gas
  - Reth (Dragan): does not fully understand it yet, will review before ACDC
  - ethrex: also needs to review
- Timeline concern: if the change is adopted, it could potentially delay Sepolia fork from end of September to end of October, jeopardizing a December mainnet target
- Decision deferred to ACDC Thursday; Maria to post discussion threads on Discord (EL R&D channel) requesting client opinions within 1-2 days
  - Goal: arrive at ACDC with decision already made, not rehash the discussion
- Dragan requested a worked example with concrete gas numbers (similar to the Svalbard examples); Maria agreed to provide one
- Spencer noted the 8037 R&D channel could be used for async discussion
